+
+Checked 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore). The primary printed source is
+O. T. Johnson, *A de Bruijn identity for symmetric stable laws*,
+arXiv:1310.2045 (2013), Section 7, pp. 16--17. The arXiv source and PDF were
+both inspected. Searches covered the arXiv API and full search, Crossref,
+the Semantic Scholar and zbMATH records/forward citations already inspected
+in the 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 passes recorded in `literature_check.md`,
+and exact-title/phrase queries for later stable-MMSE, de Bruijn, and
+nonsymmetric-stable entropy work. The live Semantic Scholar endpoint returned
+HTTP 429 and the live zbMATH endpoint returned HTTP 422 in this pass; those
+failures are not represented as successful searches. No later source located
+in the completed searches claims to settle any of the three questions below.
+This is evidence of current status, not a proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Three Printed Open Problems
+
+1. **Johnson, Open Problem 1 (MMSE-score projection).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to prove a corresponding result for the MMSE
+   score $\rho^M$ of Definition 3.1." Here "corresponding" refers to the
+   preceding conditional-expectation (projection) identity for the Fisher
+   score. **No later source located.**
+
+2. **Johnson, Open Problem 4 (integral representation).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to provide a similar representation of
+   $D(f \Vert g_s^{(\alpha)})$ as an integral, using (17)."
+   **No later source located. Finite-variance Cauchy case proved** in
+   Theorem `thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation` of this manuscript;
+   the general symmetric-stable question remains open in the searched record.
+
+3. **Johnson, Open Problem 6 (remove symmetry).** Exact quote:
+   "Finally, it would be of interest to extend all this work to more general
+   (non-symmetric) families of stable laws, removing restrictions on the
+   parameterization made in Definition 2.1." **No later source located.**
+
+## Machinery-to-Problem Map
+
+- Problem 1: the paper has translate-mixture quotients and the two-solution
+  Bregman derivative (`prop:compact-window-bregman-identity`), but no MMSE
+  score convolution formula. The missing object is precisely a conditional
+  projection identity for Johnson's $\rho^M$; none of the Laurent, tail-energy,
+  or RKHS estimates supplies it.
+- Problem 4: `prop:compact-window-bregman-identity` already differentiates
+  relative entropy for two simultaneous Cauchy semigroup solutions, while
+  `thm:poisson-kl-doob-tail` closes the large-time endpoint. The missing step
+  was to conjugate Johnson's interpolation to
+  $(P_q*\mu,P_q*P_s)$ and close the $q\downarrow0$ endpoint. The new theorem
+  proves exactly that for every finite-variance input, with extended-valued
+  relative entropy allowed.
+- Problem 6: the stable-kernel theorems use isotropic symmetric densities and
+  the Bregman proof uses a symmetric jump kernel. A skew-stable heat kernel,
+  its nonsymmetric generator/adjoint pairing, and replacement domain bounds
+  are all missing. Symmetry is structural in the current proof, not cosmetic.
+
+## Routes B, C, and D
+
+- **B (standard objects):** the canonical standard-object map is the exact
+  dilation conjugacy between Johnson's Cauchy interpolation and the Cauchy
+  convolution semigroup. The Cayley chart also maps the Cauchy law to Haar
+  measure, but the resulting Laurent modes remain computational machinery,
+  not a separate standard-object theorem. The isotropic stable heat kernels
+  in the moment-threshold theorem are already standard objects.
+- **C (hypotheses):** finite variance is used to obtain a compact quotient
+  range and the $q\to\infty$ endpoint in the new proof. It may be stronger
+  than necessary, but removing it requires a finite-entropy domain theorem
+  beyond the present cutoff argument. Symmetry/isotropy is essential to the
+  current Green pairing. Regular variation is essential only for the stated
+  missing-top-moment boundary limit, not for the law-by-law stable tail
+  decomposition.
+- **D (sharpness/converses):** the paper already has a matching counterexample
+  below the uniform stable moment exponent and an iff tail-energy criterion.
+  The plausible unclosed converse is the higher-order analytic moment
+  hierarchy; the nonzero formal top moment proves polynomial-domain
+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.
+
+## Selection
+
+Route A, Johnson Open Problem 4, has the best probability-impact product
+because the required flow is canonically present and both endpoints can be
+closed. The proved result is explicitly the finite-variance Cauchy case, not
+a solution of the full symmetric $\alpha$-stable problem. Problems 1 and 6
+require machinery absent from the paper.

+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.

+# Tier-2 Named-Problem Audit
+
+Checked 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore). The primary printed source is
+O. T. Johnson, *A de Bruijn identity for symmetric stable laws*,
+arXiv:1310.2045 (2013), Section 7, pp. 16--17. The arXiv source and PDF were
+both inspected. Searches covered the arXiv API and full search, Crossref,
+the Semantic Scholar and zbMATH records/forward citations already inspected
+in the 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 passes recorded in `literature_check.md`,
+and exact-title/phrase queries for later stable-MMSE, de Bruijn, and
+nonsymmetric-stable entropy work. The live Semantic Scholar endpoint returned
+HTTP 429 and the live zbMATH endpoint returned HTTP 422 in this pass; those
+failures are not represented as successful searches. No later source located
+in the completed searches claims to settle any of the three questions below.
+This is evidence of current status, not a proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Three Printed Open Problems
+
+1. **Johnson, Open Problem 1 (MMSE-score projection).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to prove a corresponding result for the MMSE
+   score $\rho^M$ of Definition 3.1." Here "corresponding" refers to the
+   preceding conditional-expectation (projection) identity for the Fisher
+   score. **No later source located.**
+
+2. **Johnson, Open Problem 4 (integral representation).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to provide a similar representation of
+   $D(f \Vert g_s^{(\alpha)})$ as an integral, using (17)."
+   **No later source located. Finite-variance Cauchy case proved** in
+   Theorem `thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation` of this manuscript;
+   the general symmetric-stable question remains open in the searched record.
+
+3. **Johnson, Open Problem 6 (remove symmetry).** Exact quote:
+   "Finally, it would be of interest to extend all this work to more general
+   (non-symmetric) families of stable laws, removing restrictions on the
+   parameterization made in Definition 2.1." **No later source located.**
+
+## Machinery-to-Problem Map
+
+- Problem 1: the paper has translate-mixture quotients and the two-solution
+  Bregman derivative (`prop:compact-window-bregman-identity`), but no MMSE
+  score convolution formula. The missing object is precisely a conditional
+  projection identity for Johnson's $\rho^M$; none of the Laurent, tail-energy,
+  or RKHS estimates supplies it.
+- Problem 4: `prop:compact-window-bregman-identity` already differentiates
+  relative entropy for two simultaneous Cauchy semigroup solutions, while
+  `thm:poisson-kl-doob-tail` closes the large-time endpoint. The missing step
+  was to conjugate Johnson's interpolation to
+  $(P_q*\mu,P_q*P_s)$ and close the $q\downarrow0$ endpoint. The new theorem
+  proves exactly that for every finite-variance input, with extended-valued
+  relative entropy allowed.
+- Problem 6: the stable-kernel theorems use isotropic symmetric densities and
+  the Bregman proof uses a symmetric jump kernel. A skew-stable heat kernel,
+  its nonsymmetric generator/adjoint pairing, and replacement domain bounds
+  are all missing. Symmetry is structural in the current proof, not cosmetic.
+
+## Routes B, C, and D
+
+- **B (standard objects):** the canonical standard-object map is the exact
+  dilation conjugacy between Johnson's Cauchy interpolation and the Cauchy
+  convolution semigroup. The Cayley chart also maps the Cauchy law to Haar
+  measure, but the resulting Laurent modes remain computational machinery,
+  not a separate standard-object theorem. The isotropic stable heat kernels
+  in the moment-threshold theorem are already standard objects.
+- **C (hypotheses):** finite variance is used to obtain a compact quotient
+  range and the $q\to\infty$ endpoint in the new proof. It may be stronger
+  than necessary, but removing it requires a finite-entropy domain theorem
+  beyond the present cutoff argument. Symmetry/isotropy is essential to the
+  current Green pairing. Regular variation is essential only for the stated
+  missing-top-moment boundary limit, not for the law-by-law stable tail
+  decomposition.
+- **D (sharpness/converses):** the paper already has a matching counterexample
+  below the uniform stable moment exponent and an iff tail-energy criterion.
+  The plausible unclosed converse is the higher-order analytic moment
+  hierarchy; the nonzero formal top moment proves polynomial-domain
+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.
+
+## Selection
+
+Route A, Johnson Open Problem 4, has the best probability-impact product
+because the required flow is canonically present and both endpoints can be
+closed. The proved result is explicitly the finite-variance Cauchy case, not
+a solution of the full symmetric $\alpha$-stable problem. Problems 1 and 6
+require machinery absent from the paper.

+\begin{theorem}[Cauchy case of Johnson's integral-representation problem]%
+\label{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+Fix (s>0), and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\RR\) with finite
+second moment.  For \(q>0\) put
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\qquad u_q=h_q/g_q,
+\]
+and define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
+\[
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+:=\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2\setminus\{x=y\}}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(u_q(x),u_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\dd x\dd y .
+\]
+Then \(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\) is locally integrable on \((0,\infty)\), and,
+with relative entropy between probability measures interpreted in
+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their (x)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point (x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing
+inequality give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  Since
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\), this identity gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let (T\to\infty), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}
+
 \begin{remark}[Tail-integral coefficient transfer]
 \label{rem:no-pointwise-dissipation-from-finite-moments}
 The coefficient transfer below is formulated for tail integrals

+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their (x)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point (x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing
+inequality give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  Since
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\), this identity gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let (T\to\infty), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}
+

+# Tier-2 Named-Problem Audit
+
+Checked 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore). The primary printed source is
+O. T. Johnson, *A de Bruijn identity for symmetric stable laws*,
+arXiv:1310.2045 (2013), Section 7, pp. 16--17. The arXiv source and PDF were
+both inspected. Searches covered the arXiv API and full search, Crossref,
+the Semantic Scholar and zbMATH records/forward citations already inspected
+in the 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 passes recorded in `literature_check.md`,
+and exact-title/phrase queries for later stable-MMSE, de Bruijn, and
+nonsymmetric-stable entropy work. The live Semantic Scholar endpoint returned
+HTTP 429 and the live zbMATH endpoint returned HTTP 422 in this pass; those
+failures are not represented as successful searches. No later source located
+in the completed searches claims to settle any of the three questions below.
+This is evidence of current status, not a proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Three Printed Open Problems
+
+1. **Johnson, Open Problem 1 (MMSE-score projection).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to prove a corresponding result for the MMSE
+   score $\rho^M$ of Definition 3.1." Here "corresponding" refers to the
+   preceding conditional-expectation (projection) identity for the Fisher
+   score. **No later source located.**
+
+2. **Johnson, Open Problem 4 (integral representation).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to provide a similar representation of
+   $D(f \Vert g_s^{(\alpha)})$ as an integral, using (17)."
+   **No later source located. Finite-variance Cauchy case proved** in
+   Theorem `thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation` of this manuscript;
+   the general symmetric-stable question remains open in the searched record.
+
+3. **Johnson, Open Problem 6 (remove symmetry).** Exact quote:
+   "Finally, it would be of interest to extend all this work to more general
+   (non-symmetric) families of stable laws, removing restrictions on the
+   parameterization made in Definition 2.1." **No later source located.**
+
+## Machinery-to-Problem Map
+
+- Problem 1: the paper has translate-mixture quotients and the two-solution
+  Bregman derivative (`prop:compact-window-bregman-identity`), but no MMSE
+  score convolution formula. The missing object is precisely a conditional
+  projection identity for Johnson's $\rho^M$; none of the Laurent, tail-energy,
+  or RKHS estimates supplies it.
+- Problem 4: `prop:compact-window-bregman-identity` already differentiates
+  relative entropy for two simultaneous Cauchy semigroup solutions, while
+  `thm:poisson-kl-doob-tail` closes the large-time endpoint. The missing step
+  was to conjugate Johnson's interpolation to
+  $(P_q*\mu,P_q*P_s)$ and close the $q\downarrow0$ endpoint. The new theorem
+  proves exactly that for every finite-variance input, with extended-valued
+  relative entropy allowed.
+- Problem 6: the stable-kernel theorems use isotropic symmetric densities and
+  the Bregman proof uses a symmetric jump kernel. A skew-stable heat kernel,
+  its nonsymmetric generator/adjoint pairing, and replacement domain bounds
+  are all missing. Symmetry is structural in the current proof, not cosmetic.
+
+## Routes B, C, and D
+
+- **B (standard objects):** the canonical standard-object map is the exact
+  dilation conjugacy between Johnson's Cauchy interpolation and the Cauchy
+  convolution semigroup. The Cayley chart also maps the Cauchy law to Haar
+  measure, but the resulting Laurent modes remain computational machinery,
+  not a separate standard-object theorem. The isotropic stable heat kernels
+  in the moment-threshold theorem are already standard objects.
+- **C (hypotheses):** finite variance is used to obtain a compact quotient
+  range and the $q\to\infty$ endpoint in the new proof. It may be stronger
+  than necessary, but removing it requires a finite-entropy domain theorem
+  beyond the present cutoff argument. Symmetry/isotropy is essential to the
+  current Green pairing. Regular variation is essential only for the stated
+  missing-top-moment boundary limit, not for the law-by-law stable tail
+  decomposition.
+- **D (sharpness/converses):** the paper already has a matching counterexample
+  below the uniform stable moment exponent and an iff tail-energy criterion.
+  The plausible unclosed converse is the higher-order analytic moment
+  hierarchy; the nonzero formal top moment proves polynomial-domain
+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.
+
+## Selection
+
+Route A, Johnson Open Problem 4, has the best probability-impact product
+because the required flow is canonically present and both endpoints can be
+closed. The proved result is explicitly the finite-variance Cauchy case, not
+a solution of the full symmetric $\alpha$-stable problem. Problems 1 and 6
+require machinery absent from the paper.

+\begin{theorem}[Cauchy case of Johnson's integral-representation problem]%
+\label{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+Fix (s>0), and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\RR\) with finite
+second moment.  For \(q>0\) put
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\qquad u_q=h_q/g_q,
+\]
+and define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
+\[
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+:=\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2\setminus\{x=y\}}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(u_q(x),u_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\dd x\dd y .
+\]
+Then \(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\) is locally integrable on \((0,\infty)\), and,
+with relative entropy between probability measures interpreted in
+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their (x)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point (x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing
+inequality give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  Since
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\), this identity gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let (T\to\infty), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}

+# Tier-2 Named-Problem Audit
+
+Checked 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore). The primary printed source is
+O. T. Johnson, *A de Bruijn identity for symmetric stable laws*,
+arXiv:1310.2045 (2013), Section 7, pp. 16--17. The arXiv source and PDF were
+both inspected. Searches covered the arXiv API and full search, Crossref,
+the Semantic Scholar and zbMATH records/forward citations already inspected
+in the 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 passes recorded in `literature_check.md`,
+and exact-title/phrase queries for later stable-MMSE, de Bruijn, and
+nonsymmetric-stable entropy work. The live Semantic Scholar endpoint returned
+HTTP 429 and the live zbMATH endpoint returned HTTP 422 in this pass; those
+failures are not represented as successful searches. No later source located
+in the completed searches claims to settle any of the three questions below.
+This is evidence of current status, not a proof of absence from all literature.
+
+## Three Printed Open Problems
+
+1. **Johnson, Open Problem 1 (MMSE-score projection).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to prove a corresponding result for the MMSE
+   score $\rho^M$ of Definition 3.1." Here "corresponding" refers to the
+   preceding conditional-expectation (projection) identity for the Fisher
+   score. **No later source located.**
+
+2. **Johnson, Open Problem 4 (integral representation).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to provide a similar representation of
+   $D(f \Vert g_s^{(\alpha)})$ as an integral, using (17)."
+   **No later source located. Finite-variance Cauchy case proved** in
+   Theorem `thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation` of this manuscript;
+   the general symmetric-stable question remains open in the searched record.
+
+3. **Johnson, Open Problem 6 (remove symmetry).** Exact quote:
+   "Finally, it would be of interest to extend all this work to more general
+   (non-symmetric) families of stable laws, removing restrictions on the
+   parameterization made in Definition 2.1." **No later source located.**
+
+## Machinery-to-Problem Map
+
+- Problem 1: the paper has translate-mixture quotients and the two-solution
+  Bregman derivative (`prop:compact-window-bregman-identity`), but no MMSE
+  score convolution formula. The missing object is precisely a conditional
+  projection identity for Johnson's $\rho^M$; none of the Laurent, tail-energy,
+  or RKHS estimates supplies it.
+- Problem 4: `prop:compact-window-bregman-identity` already differentiates
+  relative entropy for two simultaneous Cauchy semigroup solutions, while
+  `thm:poisson-kl-doob-tail` closes the large-time endpoint. The missing step
+  was to conjugate Johnson's interpolation to
+  $(P_q*\mu,P_q*P_s)$ and close the $q\downarrow0$ endpoint. The new theorem
+  proves exactly that for every finite-variance input, with extended-valued
+  relative entropy allowed.
+- Problem 6: the stable-kernel theorems use isotropic symmetric densities and
+  the Bregman proof uses a symmetric jump kernel. A skew-stable heat kernel,
+  its nonsymmetric generator/adjoint pairing, and replacement domain bounds
+  are all missing. Symmetry is structural in the current proof, not cosmetic.
+
+## Routes B, C, and D
+
+- **B (standard objects):** the canonical standard-object map is the exact
+  dilation conjugacy between Johnson's Cauchy interpolation and the Cauchy
+  convolution semigroup. The Cayley chart also maps the Cauchy law to Haar
+  measure, but the resulting Laurent modes remain computational machinery,
+  not a separate standard-object theorem. The isotropic stable heat kernels
+  in the moment-threshold theorem are already standard objects.
+- **C (hypotheses):** finite variance is used to obtain a compact quotient
+  range and the $q\to\infty$ endpoint in the new proof. It may be stronger
+  than necessary, but removing it requires a finite-entropy domain theorem
+  beyond the present cutoff argument. Symmetry/isotropy is essential to the
+  current Green pairing. Regular variation is essential only for the stated
+  missing-top-moment boundary limit, not for the law-by-law stable tail
+  decomposition.
+- **D (sharpness/converses):** the paper already has a matching counterexample
+  below the uniform stable moment exponent and an iff tail-energy criterion.
+  The plausible unclosed converse is the higher-order analytic moment
+  hierarchy; the nonzero formal top moment proves polynomial-domain
+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.
+
+## Selection
+
+Route A, Johnson Open Problem 4, has the best probability-impact product
+because the required flow is canonically present and both endpoints can be
+closed. The proved result is explicitly the finite-variance Cauchy case, not
+a solution of the full symmetric $\alpha$-stable problem. Problems 1 and 6
+require machinery absent from the paper.

+\begin{theorem}[Cauchy case of Johnson's integral-representation problem]%
+\label{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+Fix (s>0), and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\RR\) with finite
+second moment.  For \(q>0\) put
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\qquad u_q=h_q/g_q,
+\]
+and define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
+\[
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+:=\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2\setminus\{x=y\}}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(u_q(x),u_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\dd x\dd y .
+\]
+Then \(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\) is locally integrable on \((0,\infty)\), and,
+with relative entropy between probability measures interpreted in
+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their (x)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point (x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing
+inequality give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  Since
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\), this identity gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let (T\to\infty), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}
+

 \label{rem:no-pointwise-dissipation-from-finite-moments}
 The coefficient transfer below is formulated for tail integrals

+The same domain theorem also resolves the finite-variance Cauchy case of
+Johnson's integral-representation problem
+\cite[Open Problem~4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn}.  If \(s>0\), \(\mu\) has
+finite second moment, and
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,
+\]
+then Theorem~\ref{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} proves
+\[
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(h_q(x)/g_q(x),h_q(y)/g_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}
+\dd x\dd y\dd q .
+\]
+This follows from the exact dilation conjugacy
+\(q=st/(1-t)\) for Johnson's interpolation
+\((1-t)X+tZ_s\).  The statement is restricted to \(\alpha=1\) and does not
+claim the general symmetric-stable problem.
 \end{maintheorem}

+=\int_t^\infty\mathcal I_\nu(s)\,\dd s.
+\]
+This domain closure also gives a nonnegative integral representation of
+\(D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)\) for every finite-variance input in the Cauchy case
+of Johnson's stable de Bruijn problem.
+\end{abstract}

+\begin{theorem}[Cauchy case of Johnson's integral-representation problem]%
+\label{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+Fix (s>0), and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\RR\) with finite
+second moment.  For \(q>0\) put
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\qquad u_q=h_q/g_q,
+\]
+and define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
+\[
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+:=\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2\setminus\{x=y\}}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(u_q(x),u_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\dd x\dd y .
+\]
+Then \(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\) is locally integrable on \((0,\infty)\), and,
+with relative entropy between probability measures interpreted in
+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their (x)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point (x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing
+inequality give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  Since
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\), this identity gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let (T\to\infty), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}
+

 \label{rem:no-pointwise-dissipation-from-finite-moments}
 The coefficient transfer below is formulated for tail integrals

 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(h_t\|g_t)=\int_t^\infty \mathcal I_\nu(s)\,\dd s .

+The same domain theorem also resolves the finite-variance Cauchy case of
+Johnson's integral-representation problem
+\cite[Open Problem~4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn}.  If \(s>0\), \(\mu\) has
+finite second moment, and
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,
+\]
+then Theorem~\ref{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} proves
+\[
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(h_q(x)/g_q(x),h_q(y)/g_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}
+\dd x\dd y\dd q .
+\]
+This follows from the exact dilation conjugacy
+\(q=st/(1-t)\) for Johnson's interpolation
+\((1-t)X+tZ_s\).  The statement is restricted to \(\alpha=1\) and does not
+claim the general symmetric-stable problem.
 \end{maintheorem}

Put\n\\[\nh_t:=P_t*\\nu,\n\\qquad\ng_t(x):=P_t(x-\\bar{\\gamma}).\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\nD_{\\mathrm{KL}}(h_t\\|g_t)\\longrightarrow0\n\\qquad(t\\to\\infty).\n\\]\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nWrite $X_c=\\gamma-\\bar{\\gamma}$ and $x=\\bar{\\gamma}+ty$.  Since\n$g_t(\\bar{\\gamma}+ty)=(\\pi t)^{-1}(1+y^2)^{-1}$,\n\\[\nu_t(\\bar{\\gamma}+ty):=\\frac{h_t(\\bar{\\gamma}+ty)}{g_t(\\bar{\\gamma}+ty)}\n=\\int_{\\RR}\\frac{1+y^2}{1+(y-X_c/t)^2}\\dd\\nu(\\gamma).\n\\]\nFor $A>0$ decompose $\\nu=\\nu_A+\\nu_A^c$ according to\n$|X_c|\\le A$ and $|X_c|>A$.  The elementary kernel bound\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:second-moment-kl-kernel-bound}\n\\frac{1+y^2}{1+(y-\\varepsilon)^2}\n\\le 2(1+\\varepsilon^2)\n\\qquad(y,\\varepsilon\\in\\RR)\n\\end{equation}\nimplies\n\\[\n0\\le u_{t,A}^c(y):=\\int_{|X_c|>A}\n\\frac{1+y^2}{1+(y-X_c/t)^2}\\dd\\nu(\\gamma)\n\\le 2\\int_{|X_c|>A}\\left(1+\\frac{X_c^2}{t^2}\\right)\\dd\\nu(\\gamma).\n\\]\nHence, for $t\\ge1$,\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:second-moment-kl-tail-sup}\n\\sup_y u_{t,A}^c(y)\n\\le 2\\nu(|X_c|>A)+2\\int_{|X_c|>A}X_c^2\\dd\\nu .\n\\end{equation}\n\nThe bounded part has total mass $m_A:=\\nu(|X_c|\\le A)$ and first centred\nmoment $b_A:=\\int_{|X_c|\\le A}X_c\\dd\\nu$.  The exact expansion\n\\[\n\\frac{1+y^2}{1+(y-\\varepsilon)^2}\n=1+\\frac{2y}{1+y^2}\\varepsilon\n+\\frac{(3y^2-1)\\varepsilon^2-2y\\varepsilon^3}\n{(1+y^2)(1+(y-\\varepsilon)^2)}\n\\]\nshows that, for each fixed $A$,\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:bounded-truncated-quotient-limit}\nu_{t,A}(y):=\\int_{|X_c|\\le A}\n\\frac{1+y^2}{1+(y-X_c/t)^2}\\dd\\nu(\\gamma)\n=m_A+\\frac{2yb_A}{t(1+y^2)}+O_A(t^{-2})\n\\end{equation}\nuniformly in~$y$.  Since\n$b_A=-\\int_{|X_c|>A}X_c\\dd\\nu$, Cauchy--Schwarz gives\n\\[\n|b_A|\\le \\left(\\int_{|X_c|>A}X_c^2\\dd\\nu\\right)^{1/2}.\n\\]\nCombining this with\n\\eqref{eq:second-moment-kl-tail-sup} and\n\\eqref{eq:bounded-truncated-quotient-limit} yields the needed two-sided\nuniform estimate explicitly.  Put\n\\[\nq_A:=\\nu(|X_c|>A),\\qquad\nr_A:=\\int_{|X_c|>A}X_c^2\\dd\\nu,\\qquad\n\\eta_A(t):=\\sup_y |u_{t,A}(y)-m_A|.\n\\]\nThen \\(\\eta_A(t)\\to0\\) for each fixed \\(A\\), and for \\(t\\ge1\\)\n\\[\n-\\eta_A(t)-q_A\n\\le u_t(\\bar\\gamma+ty)-1\n\\le \\eta_A(t)+q_A+\\sup_z u_{t,A}^c(z)\n\\le \\eta_A(t)+3q_A+2r_A\n\\]\nuniformly in \\(y\\).  Hence\n\\[\n\\limsup_{t\\to\\infty}\\|u_t-1\\|_{L^\\infty(\\RR)}\n\\le 3\\nu(|X_c|>A)+2\\int_{|X_c|>A}X_c^2\\dd\\nu .\n\\]\nLetting $A\\to\\infty$ gives $\\|u_t-1\\|_\\infty\\to0$.\n\nFor all sufficiently large $t$ we therefore have\n$|u_t-1|\\le1/2$.  With $\\delta_t=u_t-1$ and using\n$\\int g_t\\delta_t=\\int(h_t-g_t)=0$,\n\\[\nD_{\\mathrm{KL}}(h_t\\|g_t)\n=\\int_{\\RR}g_t\\bigl((1+\\delta_t)\\log(1+\\delta_t)-\\delta_t\\bigr)\\dd x\n\\le 2\\|\\delta_t\\|_\\infty^2,\n\\]\nbecause $(1+s)\\log(1+s)-s\\le2s^2$ for $|s|\\le1/2$.  The right-hand side\ntends to zero.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Compact-window quotient bounds and Bregman majorant]%\n\\label{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain}\n\\label{thm:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain}\n\\label{lem:single-compact-window-bregman-majorant-constants}\n\\label{lem:bregman-kernel-l1-cutoff-removal}\nLet \\(0<a<b<\\infty\\), and let \\(\\nu\\) be a probability measure on~\\(\\RR\\)\nwith mean \\(\\bar{\\gamma}\\) and finite centred second moment\n\\[\n\\mu_2:=\\int_{\\RR}(\\gamma-\\bar{\\gamma})^2\\dd\\nu(\\gamma).\n\\]\nFor\n\\[\nh_t=P_t*\\nu,\\qquad g_t=P_t(\\cdot-\\bar{\\gamma}),\\qquad u_t=h_t/g_t,\n\\qquad t\\in[a,b],\n\\]\nput\n\\[\nm:=\\frac{1}{2(1+\\mu_2/a^2)},\\qquad\nM:=2+\\frac{2\\mu_2}{a^2},\\qquad\nL:=3a^{-1}\\bigl(1+\\mu_2/a^2\\bigr).\n\\]\nThen, for all \\(t\\in[a,b]\\) and \\(x,y\\in\\RR\\),\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:matched-poisson-quotient-domain-mML}\nm\\le u_t(x)\\le M,\\qquad\n|u_t(x)-u_t(y)|\\le L|x-y|.\n\\end{equation}\nConsequently \\(\\log u_t\\) is bounded and Lipschitz uniformly on\n\\([a,b]\\). It does not settle that problem for\ngeneral symmetric stable index \\(\\alpha\\).\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nLet \\(m=\\int x\\,\\mu(\\dd x)\\), and set\n\\[\nA_q(x):=\\frac{(P_q*\\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\\qquad\nB_q(x):=\\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.\n\\]\nThen \\(u_q=A_q/B_q\\).  On each compact interval\n\\([a,b]\\Subset(0,\\infty)\\), Lemma\n\\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive\ncompact range and one Lipschitz constant for \\(A_q\\).  Moreover\n\\[\nB_q(x)=\\frac{q+s}{q}\n\\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.\n\\]\nThe function on the right, its reciprocal, and their (x)-derivatives are\nbounded uniformly for \\((q,x)\\in[a,b]\\times\\RR\\).  Indeed, after adjoining\nthe point (x=\\infty\\), they are continuous rational functions on the\ncompact set \\([a,b]\\times\\overline\\RR\\), and neither denominator vanishes.\nThe quotient rule therefore gives constants\n\\(0<c_{a,b}\\le C_{a,b}<\\infty\\) and \\(L_{a,b}<\\infty\\) such that\n\\[\nc_{a,b}\\le u_q(x)\\le C_{a,b},\\qquad\n|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.\n\\]\nProposition~\\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two\ninitial measures \\(\\mu\\) and \\(P_s(x)\\dd x\\), now shows that\n\\[\nH(q):=D_{\\rm KL}(P_q*\\mu\\|P_{q+s})\n\\]\nis absolutely continuous on \\([a,b]\\), that\n\\(\\mathcal J_{\\mu,s}\\in L^1([a,b])\\), and that\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}\nH\'(q)=-\\mathcal J_{\\mu,s}(q)\n\\quad\\text{for a.e. }q\\in[a,b].\n\\end{equation}\n\nWe next close both endpoints separately.  As \\(q\\downarrow0\\),\n\\(P_q*\\mu\\Rightarrow\\mu\\) and \\(P_{q+s}\\Rightarrow P_s\\).  The variational\nformula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak\nconvergence, whereas convolution by \\(P_q\\) and the data-processing\ninequality give\n\\[\nH(q)=D_{\\rm KL}(P_q*\\mu\\|P_q*P_s)\n\\le D_{\\rm KL}(\\mu\\|P_s).\n\\]\nConsequently\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}\nH(q)\\longrightarrow D_{\\rm KL}(\\mu\\|P_s)\n\\qquad(q\\downarrow0)\n\\end{equation}\nin the extended interval \\([0,\\infty]\\).\n\nAt the other endpoint, Lemma~\\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with\n\\(L=2\\) gives \\(\\|A_q-1\\|_\\infty=O(q^{-2})\\).  If\n\\(y=(x-m)/q\\), \\(\\sigma=s/q\\), and \\(\\delta=m/q\\), then\n\\[\nB_q(x)=(1+\\sigma)\n\\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\\sigma)^2+(y+\\delta)^2}.\n\\]\nThe difference of its numerator and denominator is\n\\(\\sigma y^2-2\\delta y-\\sigma-\\sigma^2-\\delta^2\\).  Since\n\\(|y|/(1+y^2)\\le1/2\\), this identity gives\n\\(\\|B_q-1\\|_\\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\\). This proves\n\\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either\nside is infinite.\n\nFinally, dilation by \\((1-t)^{-1}\\) sends the law of \\(X_t\\) to\n\\[\n\\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\\mu\n\\]\nand sends \\(P_s\\) to\n\\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same\nbimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving\n\\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since\n\\(\\dd q/\\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\\), the chain rule and\n\\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give\n\\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{remark}[Tail-integral coefficient transfer]\n\\label{rem:no-pointwise-dissipation-from-finite-moments}\nThe coefficient transfer below is formulated for tail integrals\n\\(\\int_t^\\infty\\mathcal I_\\nu(s)\\dd s\\) and fixed multiplicative-window\naverages.  Passing from a tail expansion for the primitive\n\\(H(t)=\\int_t^\\infty\\mathcal I_\\nu(s)\\dd s\\), even with a full finite-moment\ncoefficient hierarchy, to pointwise asymptotics for \\(\\mathcal I_\\nu(t)\\)\nrequires extra differentiated-remainder input.\n\nFor example, if the centred law is compactly supported, say\n\\(|\\gamma-\\bar{\\gamma}|\\le M\\), then for each fixed retained order \\(L\\) and\nall \\(t>2M\\) the Cayley generating function gives the uniformly convergent\nexpansion, with \\(\\mu_n=\\EE(\\gamma-\\bar{\\gamma})^n\\),\n\\[\n\\frac{(P_t*\\nu)(\\bar{\\gamma}+ty)}{P_t(ty)}-1\n=\\sum_{n=2}^{L}\\mu_nu_n(y)t^{-n}+\\rho_{L,t}(y),\n\\qquad\n\\rho_{L,t}=\\sum_{n>L}\\mu_nu_n(y)t^{-n}.\n\\]\nThe same uniform majorant gives\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\|\\rho_{L,t}\\|_{L^\\infty}\n+\\|\\rho_{L,t}\\|_{L^1(\\omega)}\n+\\|t\\partial_t\\rho_{L,t}\\|_{L^\\infty}\n+\\|t\\partial_t\\rho_{L,t}\\|_{L^1(\\omega)}\n=O_\\nu(t^{-(L+1)}).\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\nUnder such a differentiated remainder bound, one may\ndifferentiate the finite quotient expansion and combine it with\n\\eqref{eq:relative-entropy-integrated-dissipation}; this auxiliary\nobservation requires more than the finite-moment coefficient hierarchy.\n\\end{remark}\n\n\\begin{proposition}[Dissipation-tail and window-average coefficient transfer]%\n\\label{prop:dissipation-tail-coefficient-expansion}\nLet \\(N\\ge2\\), and assume that \\(\\nu\\) has finite centred\n\\((2N-2)\\)th absolute moment.
