+\begin{theorem}[Cauchy case of Johnson's integral-representation problem]%
+\label{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+Fix \(s>0\), and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\RR\) with finite
+second moment.  For \(q>0\) put
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\qquad u_q=h_q/g_q,
+\]
+and define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
+\[
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+:=\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2\setminus\{x=y\}}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(u_q(x),u_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\dd x\dd y .
+\]
+Then \(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\) is locally integrable on \((0,\infty)\), and,
+with relative entropy between probability measures interpreted in
+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).  Whenever Johnson's score pairing
+in his equation~(17) is defined, comparison with
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} identifies that pairing
+with the displayed nonnegative Bregman density after the change of variables.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their \(x\)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point \(x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing inequality
+give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  For all large \(q\),
+\((1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2\ge(1+y^2)/3\), and
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\).  This identity therefore gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let \(T\to\infty\), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}
+

 \label{rem:no-pointwise-dissipation-from-finite-moments}
 The coefficient transfer below is formulated for tail integrals

+The same domain theorem also resolves the finite-variance Cauchy case of
+Johnson's integral-representation problem
+\cite[Open Problem~4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn}.  If \(s>0\), \(\mu\) has
+finite second moment, and
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,
+\]
+then Theorem~\ref{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} proves
+\[
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(h_q(x)/g_q(x),h_q(y)/g_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}
+\dd x\dd y\dd q .
+\]
+This follows from the exact dilation conjugacy
+\(q=st/(1-t)\) for Johnson's interpolation
+\((1-t)X+tZ_s\).  The statement is restricted to \(\alpha=1\) and does not
+claim the general symmetric-stable problem.
 \end{maintheorem}

Proposition~\\ref{thm:sharp-moment-equivalence-hierarchy}\nis only this algebraic polynomial-domain minimality statement.  In particular,\nfor \\(m\\ge3\\) it is not an unconditional converse for the entropy remainder.\n\nThe second theorem is multidimensional and finite-moment.  For\n\\(L\\ge d+1\\), finite centred \\(L\\)-moment closes the large-translation\nremainder in the matched radial Poisson quotient, gives an explicit\n\\(L^\\infty\\cap L^1(\\Omega_d)\\) jet, supplies the large-\\(t\\)\nentropy-existence package, and hence gives the tensor KL expansion through\norder \\(L+2\\).  The two-region expression is retained as the quantitative\nremainder bound; in this range the precise statement is the equivalence\n\\(\\mathcal R_{d,L}(t)=o(t^{-L})\\) for the two-region functional defined in\n\\path{sec_entropy_core_main.tex}, Definition ``Two-region remainder\nfunctional,\'\' and the finite\n\\(L\\)-moment assumption.\nThe restriction \\(L\\ge d+1\\) is sharp for this \\(L^\\infty\\) quotient\ntopology, as shown by the spike construction below.  It is not claimed to be\nnecessary for the leading KL coefficient in a weaker \\(L^2(\\Omega_d)\\) or\nentropy topology.  Section~\\ref{sec:verified-A2-results} treats those weaker\ntopologies separately: the sharp moment exponent for the \\(L^2\\) quotient is\n\\(\\max\\{2,(d+1)/2\\}\\); finite covariance is the exact leading-KL threshold\nfor \\(d\\le3\\); and finite covariance fails to control the leading KL scale\nfor every \\(d\\ge4\\).  For every isotropic strictly \\(\\alpha\\)-stable\nkernel, the optimal uniform sufficient exponent among finite\nabsolute-moment assumptions is\n\\[\n p_{\\alpha,d}=\\max\\left\\{2,\n \\frac{4(d+\\alpha)}{d+\\alpha+4}\\right\\},\n\\]\nwith the endpoint on the sufficient side; see\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:high-dimensional-kl-moment-threshold}.  This optimization\nover moment classes is not a law-by-law necessity statement when\n\\(d+\\alpha>4\\).  The exact finite-covariance interface is instead supplied\nby Theorem~\\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition}.  For a centred law put\n\\[\n V_s^\\nu(y)=\\int_{\\{|x|>s\\}}\n \\frac{p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y-x/s)}{p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)}\\,\\nu(\\dd x).\n\\]\nThen, without regular variation, absolute continuity, or a moment above\norder two,\n\\[\n H_{\\alpha,d}(s)=\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)s^{-4}\n +\\int\\Phi(V_s^\\nu)\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}+o(s^{-4}).\n\\]\nThus the covariance coefficient is attained exactly when the nonlinear raw\ntail energy is \\(o(s^{-4})\\).  When \\(d+\\alpha\\le4\\), the uniform exponent\nis two and this tail condition follows from finite covariance; when\n\\(d+\\alpha>4\\), it is the additional law-by-law condition not expressible by\nthe uniform moment exponent alone.  The infinite\ncritical-moment boundary is genuinely different: Theorem\n\\ref{thm:critical-vague-tail-nonidentifiability} constructs two laws with the\nsame smooth multivariate regularly varying tail data and the same covariance,\none attaining the covariance coefficient and the other having unbounded\nscaled entropy along a subsequence.\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:covariance-proxy-defect-decomposition} gives an\nasymptotically exact\nfinite-covariance characterization of this distinction.  If\n\\(k_{\\Sigma,t}\\) denotes the positive Poisson density obtained by adjoining\nthe normalized quadratic mode \\(t^{-2}b_\\Sigma\\) to the matched reference,\nthen\n\\[\n t^4H_d(t)=\\mathcal Q_d(\\Sigma)\n +t^4D_{\\rm KL}(h_t\\|k_{\\Sigma,t})+o(1).\n\\]\nThus attainment of the covariance coefficient is equivalent to the\nvanishing of the complete nonlinear proxy defect.  This statement requires\nonly finite covariance and does not impose a density or tail regularity on\nthe original law.\nThe leading multidimensional covariance formula is deliberately read through\nthis analytic route.  Finite covariance alone determines the bounded quadratic\nmode \\(b_\\Sigma\\) and the algebraic number \\(\\mathcal Q_d(\\Sigma)\\), but it\ndoes not by itself make \\(\\mathcal Q_d(\\Sigma)\\) the coefficient of\n\\eqref{eq:intro-main-functional}.  It becomes the leading KL coefficient only\nafter a quotient/existence bridge is in force, for example the\n\\((\\mathrm{MPJ}_{d,L})+(\\mathrm{EX}_{d,L})\\) package supplied here by\nfinite \\(L\\)-moment with \\(L\\ge d+1\\), or the separate second-order quotient\ncriterion stated in Section~\\ref{sec:entropy-asymptotics}.\n\nThe nearest fractional-diffusion prior art is\nIshige--Kawakami--Michihisa\n\\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} and the refined follow-up\n\\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2022RefinedFractional}.  For every\n\\(0<\\alpha<2\\) and weighted moment order \\(K\\ge0\\), those works subtract\nmoment-weighted derivatives of the stable heat kernel and prove scaled\n\\(L^q\\) and weighted \\(L^1\\) remainder decay for the resulting density\nexpansion, including inhomogeneous and nonlinear refinements.  They do not\ncontrol the matched density quotient in\n\\(L^{q_{\\alpha,d}}(p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\dd y)\\) or transfer that critical\nestimate through relative entropy; those are the steps that produce\n\\(p_{\\alpha,d}\\) here.  They also do not retain the unexpanded translate\nmixture beyond the smoothing scale as the nonlinear entropy energy in\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition}.\n\n\\ifdefined\\JFAArticleMain\nThe full domain-closure motivation and comparison with the general\ntwo-solution Bregman calculus are in \\path{sec_introduction.tex}, the\nparagraphs preceding ``Theorems,\'\' collected by\n\\path{supplement_relocated_support.tex}.\n\\else\nThe third theorem is a domain-and-endpoint result for the standard\nsimultaneous-semigroup relative-entropy calculus.  For a symmetric jump\ngenerator\n\\[\n(L_Jf)(x)=\\int\\{f(y)-f(x)\\}J(x,y)\\,\\dd y,\n\\qquad J(x,y)=J(y,x),\n\\]\nand sufficiently regular positive solutions\n\\(\\partial_t h_t=L_Jh_t\\), \\(\\partial_t g_t=L_Jg_t\\), set\n\\(u_t=h_t/g_t\\).  The general generator identity is\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:intro-general-two-solution-generator-identity}\n-\\frac{\\dd}{\\dd t}D_{\\rm KL}(h_t\\|g_t)\n=\\frac12\\iint J(x,y)\n\\left[g_t(x)\\Lambda(u_t(x),u_t(y))\n+g_t(y)\\Lambda(u_t(y),u_t(x))\\right]\\dd x\\dd y.\n\\end{equation}\nBy exchanging \\(x\\) and \\(y\\) in the second term, the right side equals\n\\[\n\\iint J(x,y)g_t(x)\\Lambda(u_t(x),u_t(y))\\dd x\\dd y.\n\\]\nThis is the logarithmic relative-\\(\\Phi\\)-entropy identity for two solutions\nof the same symmetric jump semigroup; its Bregman differentiation is not\nclaimed as new \\cite{Chafai2004PhiEntropies,BakryCoulhonLedouxSaloffCoste1995}.\n\nUnder finite centred variance, Theorem~\\ref{thm:main-C} verifies that the\nmoving matched Cauchy quotient lies in the domain of this identity on every\ncompact time window, with the generator normalized as the symmetric\n\\(1\\)-stable Cauchy generator\n\\cite{Feller1971,Bertoin1996LevyProcesses,Sato1999LevyProcesses,\nApplebaum2009LevyProcesses,Kwasnicki2017}.  The KL functional is then the\ntail integral of the resulting nonlocal dissipation.  Here both the quotient\n\\[\nu_t=\\frac{h_t}{g_t}\n\\]\nand the reference density \\(g_t=P_t(\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma)\\) move with \\(t\\).\nThe logarithmic chain rule therefore first gives the two-pair identity\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:intro-two-pair-chain-rule}\nH\'(t)=\\langle \\log u_t,\\partial_t h_t\\rangle\n      -\\langle u_t-1,\\partial_t g_t\\rangle,\n\\qquad H(t)=D_{\\rm KL}(h_t\\|g_t),\n\\end{equation}\nnot a single fixed-reference Dirichlet form.  Applying the Cauchy Green\nformula separately to the pairs \\((h_t,\\log u_t)\\) and \\((g_t,u_t)\\), and\nusing \\(\\int\\partial_tg_t=0\\), produces the algebraic difference\n\\[\n(\\rho_xa-\\rho_yb)(\\log a-\\log b)-(\\rho_x-\\rho_y)(a-b)\n=\\rho_x\\Lambda(a,b)+\\rho_y\\Lambda(b,a),\n\\]\nwhere \\(a=u_t(x)\\), \\(b=u_t(y)\\), \\(\\rho_x=g_t(x)\\),\n\\(\\rho_y=g_t(y)\\), and\n\\(\\Lambda(a,b)=a\\log(a/b)-a+b\\).  This is the logarithmic case of the\nCsisz{\\\'a}r--Morimoto--Ali--Silvey \\(f\\)-divergence/Bregman calculus\n\\cite{AliSilvey1966Divergence,Csiszar1967,Morimoto1963Markov,\nVajda1989TheoryDivergence,Bregman1967}.  The actual increment is to justify\nthese formal pairings on the noncompact Cauchy state space: finite variance\nyields compact-window upper and lower quotient bounds, valid Green cutoffs,\nand integrable domination of the Bregman kernel.  The separate endpoint proof\n\\(H(T)\\to0\\) then permits integration to infinity.\n\nThe coefficient-domain and boundary-layer increments are separate from\nthat dissipation identity.  Stable-semigroup de Bruijn and Hardy--Stein formulas identify an\nentropy derivative or an integrated Bregman/Dirichlet form\n\\cite{DeBruijn1953,HirataNemotoYoshida2012RelativeEntropy,\nYoshida2017RelativeEntropyDiffusion,BanuelosBogdanLuks2016HardyStein,\nGutowski2023HardySteinPureJump,\nBogdanGutowskiPietruskaPaluba2025PolarizedHardyStein,\nJohnson2013StableDeBruijn,Toscani2016StableEntropy,\nBobkovChistyakovGotze2013StableEntropy}.  They do not determine the large-time\ncoefficient residual for a fixed input law against a moving matched Cauchy\nreference.  The analytic increments here are the unconditional bounded-mode\nconverse at the variance threshold and the signed,\ntruncated-moment-normalized residual within the stated regularly varying\nclass.  The all-order Cayley--Laurent calculation instead supplies a finite\npolynomial-evaluation algorithm and its minimal universal absolute-moment\nassumption.\n\\fi\n\n\\subsection*{Theorems}\\label{subsec:main-results}\n\n\\begin{maintheorem}{Analytic variance threshold and coefficient-domain minimality}\n\\label{thm:main-A}\nLet \\(\\nu\\) be a probability law on \\(\\RR\\) with finite mean\n\\(\\bar\\gamma\\), and put \\(X_c=\\gamma-\\bar\\gamma\\).  No variance or tail\nassumption is imposed at this point.  Set\n\\[\nH(t)=D_{\\mathrm{KL}}\\bigl(P_t*\\nu\\,\\|\\,P_t(\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma)\\bigr)\n\\]\nwith the extended nonnegative convention for relative entropy.  Then\n\\[\n\\EE X_c^2<\\infty\n\\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n\\limsup_{t\\to\\infty}t^4H(t)<\\infty .\n\\]\nIf the variance is finite, then \\(H(t)<\\infty\\) for every \\(t>0\\) and\n\\[\n\\lim_{t\\to\\infty}t^4H(t)=\\frac{(\\EE X_c^2)^2}{8};\n\\]\nif it is infinite, then\n\\[\n\\lim_{t\\to\\infty}t^4H(t)=+\\infty\n\\]\nin the extended sense.  No compact-support, exponential-tail, or\nregular-variation hypothesis is used in this equivalence.\n\nFor the higher universal coefficients, the conclusion is algebraic rather\nthan an unconditional analytic converse.  For every \\(m\\ge3\\), let\n\\(A_{2m}^{\\rm form}\\) be the reduced universal polynomial defined by the\nconstant-term rule below.  Then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:main-A-moment-equivalence}\nA_{2m}^{\\rm form}\n=\\kappa_m\\mathfrak m_2\\mathfrak m_{2m-2}\n+P_m(\\mathfrak m_2,\\ldots,\\mathfrak m_{2m-3}),\n\\qquad\n\\kappa_m=(-1)^m(m-1)2^{-2m+2}\\ne0,\n\\end{equation}\nAt \\(m=2\\), \\(A_4^{\\rm form}=\\mathfrak m_2^2/8\\).  Consequently, for every\n\\(m\\ge2\\),\n\\(\\EE|X_c|^{2m-2}<\\infty\\) is sufficient for the canonical Lebesgue\nevaluation of every monomial, and is minimal among absolute-moment\nassumptions that guarantee evaluation uniformly over all centred probability\nlaws.  This statement uses the deliberately specified polynomial-evaluation\ndomain of Definition~\\ref{def:canonical-coefficient-finiteness}; for\n\\(m\\ge3\\) it is not an unconditional converse for the entropy remainder.\n\nThe supporting coefficient expansion has the exact moment hypothesis as\nfollows.  Let \\(N\\ge2\\), put \\(L=2N-2\\), and assume now that\n\\(\\EE|X_c|^L<\\infty\\).  With\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n  \\mu_n&=\\int_{\\RR} X_c^n\\,\\dd\\nu(\\gamma)\\qquad(2\\le n\\le L),\\\\\n  h_t&=P_t*\\nu,\\qquad\n  g_t&=P_t(\\cdot-\\bar{\\gamma}),\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\none has\n\\[\nD_{\\mathrm{KL}}(h_t\\|g_t)\n=\\sum_{m=2}^{N}A_{2m}(\\nu)t^{-2m}+o(t^{-2N}).\n\\]\nThe coefficients are part of the statement.  For \\(2\\le m\\le N\\),\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:main-A-intro-coefficients}\nA_{2m}(\\nu)=\n\\sum_{r=2}^{m}\n\\frac{(-1)^r}{r(r-1)}\n\\sum_{\\substack{n_1+\\cdots+n_r=2m\\\\ n_j\\ge2}}\n\\mu_{n_1}\\cdots\\mu_{n_r}\n\\,[z^0]\\prod_{j=1}^r Q_{n_j}(z),\n\\end{equation}\nwhere \\([z^0]\\) denotes constant Laurent coefficient and the\nCayley--Chebyshev Laurent representative is fixed by the convention\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:main-A-intro-Qn}\nQ_n(z)=2^{-n}(-\\ii)^n\n\\sum_{\\ell=1}^{n}\\binom{n-1}{\\ell-1}\n\\bigl(z^\\ell+(-1)^nz^{-\\ell}\\bigr)\n\\qquad(n\\ge1).\n\\end{equation}\nThus \\(A_{2m}(\\nu)\\) is a universal polynomial in\n\\(\\mu_2,\\ldots,\\mu_{2m-2}\\); the proof that\n\\eqref{eq:main-A-intro-coefficients} is the entropy coefficient is supplied\nby Theorem~\\ref{thm:poisson-kl-even-orders}.  All retained odd coefficients\nvanish, and the leading coefficient is\n\\[\nA_4(\\nu)=\\frac{\\mu_2^2}{8}.\n\\]\n\\end{maintheorem}\n\n\\begin{maintheorem}{Multidimensional Poisson jets and stable-kernel moment exponent}\n\\label{thm:main-B}\nLet \\(d\\ge1\\), let \\(L\\in\\NN\\) satisfy \\(L\\ge d+1\\), and let \\(\\nu\\) be a\nprobability measure on \\(\\RR^d\\) with mean \\(\\bar\\gamma\\).  Put\n\\[\nX_c=\\gamma-\\bar\\gamma .\n\\]\nAssume \\(\\EE |X_c|^L<\\infty\\).  Then the centred moments\n\\[\n\\mu_\\alpha=\\EE[X_c^\\alpha]\\qquad(|\\alpha|\\le L)\n\\]\nare finite.  The explicit two-region condition used in the quotient proof is\nonly the following one:\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\mathcal R_{d,L}(t)\n&:=t^{-(L+1)}\\EE\\!\\left[\n|X_c|^{L+1}{\\bf1}_{\\{|X_c|\\le t\\}}\\right] \\\\\n&\\quad{}+ t^{-L}\\EE\\!\\left[\n|X_c|^L{\\bf1}_{\\{|X_c|>t\\}}\\right],\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\none has, in the stated range \\(L\\ge d+1\\),\n\\[\n\\mathcal R_{d,L}(t)=o(t^{-L})\n\\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n\\EE |X_c|^L<\\infty .\n\\]\nNo broader equivalence between arbitrary two-region estimates and moment\nhypotheses is asserted.  The restriction \\(L\\ge d+1\\) is sharp for this\n\\(L^\\infty\\) quotient topology: for every integer \\(1\\le L<d+1\\), the spike\nconstruction following Theorem~\\ref{thm:second-order-quotient-kl-coefficient}\ngives a centred law with finite \\(L\\)th absolute moment whose quotient does\nnot converge uniformly to one.  This does not establish necessity for a\nleading KL coefficient under a weaker \\(L^2(\\Omega_d)\\) or entropy topology;\nthe separate sharp \\(L^2\\) result and the dimension-dependent KL statements\nare Theorems~\\ref{thm:multidim-l2-moment-threshold} and\n\\ref{thm:low-dimensional-finite-covariance-threshold}, together with\nProposition~\\ref{prop:high-dimensional-finite-covariance-obstruction} and\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:high-dimensional-kl-moment-threshold}.\nWith\n\\[\nh_t=P_t^{(d)}*\\nu,\\qquad\ng_t=P_t^{(d)}(\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma),\n\\]\none has, for all sufficiently large \\(t\\),\n\\[\nD_{\\mathrm{KL}}(h_t\\|g_t)\n=\\sum_{m=4}^{L+2}\\mathcal A_m^{(d)}(\\nu)t^{-m}\n+o(t^{-(L+2)}),\n\\]\nwhere, for \\(4\\le m\\le L+2\\),\n\\[\n\\mathcal A_m^{(d)}(\\nu)=\n\\sum_{r=2}^{\\lfloor m/2\\rfloor}\n\\frac{(-1)^r}{r(r-1)}\n\\sum_{\\substack{\\alpha_1,\\ldots,\\alpha_r\\in\\NN_0^d\\\\\n|\\alpha_1|+\\cdots+|\\alpha_r|=m\\\\\n2\\le|\\alpha_j|\\le L\\ \\mathrm{for}\\ 1\\le j\\le r}}\n\\mu_{\\alpha_1}\\cdots\\mu_{\\alpha_r}\n\\int_{\\RR^d}\\prod_{j=1}^r\nU_{\\alpha_j}^{(d)}(y)\\,\\Omega_d(\\dd y).\n\\]\nHere \\(U_\\alpha^{(d)}\\) denotes the radial Poisson Taylor mode and\n\\[\n\\Omega_d(\\dd y)\n=\\frac{\\Gamma((d+1)/2)}{\\pi^{(d+1)/2}}\n(1+|y|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\\,\\dd y\n\\]\nis the \\(t=1\\) \\(d\\)-dimensional Poisson law.  The displayed formula is a\nfinite universal tensor polynomial in the centred moments of orders\n\\(2,\\ldots,m-2\\), and all retained odd coefficients vanish.\nFor the leading retained coefficient, let\n\\[\n\\Sigma=\\EE[X_cX_c^{\\mathsf T}],\\qquad\n\\Sigma_0=\\Sigma-\\frac{\\operatorname{tr}\\Sigma}{d}I_d .\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n\\mathcal A_4^{(d)}(\\nu)=\\mathcal Q_d(\\Sigma)\n=c_d^{\\rm iso}(\\operatorname{tr}\\Sigma)^2\n+c_d^{\\rm tr}\\|\\Sigma_0\\|_{\\rm HS}^2,\n\\]\nwith\n\\[\nc_d^{\\rm iso}=\n\\frac{3(d+1)(7d+9)}\n{4d(d+3)(d+5)(d+7)},\n\\qquad\nc_d^{\\rm tr}=\n\\frac{3(d+1)(d+3)}\n{4(d+5)(d+7)} .\n\\]\nEquivalently,\n\\[\n\\mathcal Q_d(\\Sigma)\n=\\frac12\\int_{\\RR^d}b_\\Sigma(y)^2\\,\\Omega_d(\\dd y),\n\\quad\nb_\\Sigma(y)=\n\\frac{d+1}{2}\\left(\n-\\frac{\\operatorname{tr}\\Sigma}{1+|y|^2}\n+\\frac{(d+3)y^{\\mathsf T}\\Sigma y}{(1+|y|^2)^2}\n\\right).\n\\]\nSeparately, let \\(0<\\alpha<2\\) and let\n\\(p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}(x)=s^{-d}p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(x/s)\\) be any isotropic\nstrictly \\(\\alpha\\)-stable kernel.  If\n\\[\n \\EE|X_c|^{p_{\\alpha,d}}<\\infty,\n \\qquad\n p_{\\alpha,d}=\\max\\left\\{2,\n \\frac{4(d+\\alpha)}{d+\\alpha+4}\\right\\},\n\\]\nthen\n\\[\n D_{\\rm KL}\\!\\left(p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu\\,\\middle\\|\\,\n p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\mathord\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma)\\right)\n =\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)s^{-4}+o(s^{-4}),\n\\]\nwith \\(\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}\\) defined in\n\\eqref{eq:stable-leading-covariance-functional}.  The exponent is optimal\nas a uniform sufficient finite-moment hypothesis, including its endpoint;\nno smaller absolute-moment exponent works uniformly over its full moment\nclass.\n\nFor an individual centred law with finite covariance \\(\\Sigma\\), define\n\\[\n V_s^\\nu(y):=\\int_{\\{|x|>s\\}}\n \\frac{p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y-x/s)}\n      {p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)}\\,\\nu(\\dd x).\n\\]\nThen the exact law-by-law decomposition is\n\\[\n H_{\\alpha,d}(s)=\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)s^{-4}\n +\\int_{\\RR^d}\\Phi(V_s^\\nu(y))\\,\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}(\\dd y)\n +o(s^{-4}),\n\\]\nand hence\n\\[\n s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)\\longrightarrow\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)\n \\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n s^4\\int_{\\RR^d}\\Phi(V_s^\\nu)\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\\longrightarrow0.\n\\]\nThis clause assumes no regular variation, absolute continuity, or moment\nabove order two.\n\\end{maintheorem}\n\n\\begin{maintheorem}{Domain and endpoint closure for Cauchy relative entropy}\n\\label{thm:main-C}\nLet \\(\\nu\\) be a probability measure on \\(\\RR\\) with mean \\(\\bar{\\gamma}\\) and\nfinite centred second moment.  Put\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\nh_t&=P_t*\\nu,\\\\\ng_t&=P_t(\\cdot-\\bar{\\gamma}),\\\\\nu_t&=h_t/g_t .\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\nDefine the Bregman kernel by\n\\[\n\\Lambda(\\alpha,\\beta)=\\alpha\\log\\frac{\\alpha}{\\beta}-\\alpha+\\beta,\n\\]\nand define the nonlocal Bregman dissipation by the nonnegative Lebesgue\nintegral\n\\[\n\\mathcal I_\\nu(t)\n=\\frac1\\pi\\iint_{\\RR^2}\n\\frac{g_t(x)\\Lambda(u_t(x),u_t(y))}{(x-y)^2}\\dd x\\dd y ,\n\\]\nwith the diagonal ignored.  For the Cauchy jump kernel\n\\(J(x,y)=\\{\\pi(x-y)^2\\}^{-1}\\), this is exactly the right side of the\ngeneral two-solution identity displayed in \\path{sec_introduction.tex}, in the\nparagraphs preceding ``Theorems,\'\' under the label\n\\path{eq:intro-general-two-solution-generator-identity}.  The assertion is\nthat the matched quotient belongs to the required domain: \\(\\mathcal I_\\nu\\)\nis measurable and locally integrable on \\((0,\\infty)\\).  More precisely, on every compact window\n\\([a,b]\\Subset(0,\\infty)\\), the quotient \\(u_t\\) satisfies the bounded\nLipschitz estimates, Green-cutoff convergence, and integrable Bregman-kernel\ndomination recorded in\n\\path{sec_doob_phi_entropy.tex}, Proposition ``Matched-Poisson domain and\ndifferentiation package.\'\'  These bounds\njustify the general generator identity, while the separate endpoint result\n\\(D_{\\rm KL}(h_T\\|g_T)\\to0\\) justifies passage from a finite time window to\ninfinity.  Consequently, for every \\(t>0\\),\n\\[\nD_{\\mathrm{KL}}(h_t\\|g_t)=\\int_t^\\infty \\mathcal I_\\nu(s)\\,\\dd s .\n\\]\nThe same domain theorem also resolves the finite-variance Cauchy case of\nJohnson\'s integral-representation problem\n\\cite[Open Problem~4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn}.  If \\(s>0\\), \\(\\mu\\) has\nfinite second moment, and\n\\[\nh_q=P_q*\\mu,\\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\n\\]\nthen Theorem~\\ref{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} proves\n\\[\nD_{\\rm KL}(\\mu\\|P_s)\n=\\int_0^\\infty\\frac1\\pi\\iint_{\\RR^2}\n\\frac{g_q(x)\\Lambda(h_q(x)/g_q(x),h_q(y)/g_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\n\\dd x\\dd y\\dd q .\n\\]\nThis follows from the exact dilation conjugacy\n\\(q=st/(1-t)\\) for Johnson\'s interpolation\n\\((1-t)X+tZ_s\\).  The statement is restricted to \\(\\alpha=1\\) and does not\nclaim the general symmetric-stable problem.\n\\end{maintheorem}\n\n\\ifdefined\\JFAArticleMain\nThe comparison by mechanism, hypothesis ledger, and detailed organization\nguide are in \\path{sec_introduction.tex}, after the three main-theorem\nstatements, collected by \\path{supplement_relocated_support.tex}.\n\\else\n\\subsection*{Comparison by mechanism}\n\\label{subsec:intro-recent-jfa-comparison}\n\nClassical moment decompositions expand a function or convolution solution\ninto masses and derivatives of a fundamental kernel; see\nDuoandikoetxea--Zuazua \\cite{DuoandikoetxeaZuazua1992} and the subsequent\nlarge-time diffusion literature\n\\cite{EscobedoZuazua1991,IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017,\nIshigeKawakamiMichihisa2022RefinedFractional}.  In particular,\nIshige--Kawakami--Michihisa treat every \\(0<\\alpha<2\\) and every weighted\nmoment order \\(K\\ge0\\): for data in\n\\(L^1(\\RR^d,(1+|x|)^K\\dd x)\\), their Theorem~1.1 subtracts the\nmoment-weighted derivatives of the fractional heat kernel and proves the\ncorresponding scaled \\(L^q\\) and weighted \\(L^1\\) remainder decay, including\nthe range \\(K\\ge\\alpha\\) where the stable semigroup does not preserve that\nweighted space.  The refined follow-up also expands the inhomogeneous and\nnonlinear fractional-diffusion solutions.  Those results supply the\ndensity-level moment expansion. +# Tier-2 Named-Problem Audit
+
+Checked 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore). The primary printed source is
+O. T. Johnson, *A de Bruijn identity for symmetric stable laws*,
+arXiv:1310.2045 (2013), Section 7, pp. 16--17. The arXiv source and PDF were
+both inspected. Searches covered the arXiv API and full search, Crossref,
+the Semantic Scholar and zbMATH records/forward citations already inspected
+in the 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 passes recorded in `literature_check.md`,
+and exact-title/phrase queries for later stable-MMSE, de Bruijn, and
+nonsymmetric-stable entropy work. The live Semantic Scholar endpoint returned
+HTTP 429 and the live zbMATH endpoint returned HTTP 422 in this pass; those
+failures are not represented as successful searches. No later source located
+in the completed searches claims to settle any of the three questions below.
+This is evidence of current status, not a proof of absence from all literature.
+The deceptively close title M. Hirata, A. Nemoto, and H. Yoshida, *An Integral
+Representation of the Relative Entropy*, Entropy 14 (2012), 1469--1477,
+DOI 10.3390/e14081469, was also checked: its abstract and theorem regime are
+Gaussian heat flow, not Johnson's stable interpolation.
+
+## Three Printed Open Problems
+
+1. **Johnson, Open Problem 1 (MMSE-score projection).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to prove a corresponding result for the MMSE score
+   $\rho^M$ of Definition 3.1." Here "corresponding" refers to the
+   preceding conditional-expectation (projection) identity for the Fisher
+   score. **No later source located.**
+
+2. **Johnson, Open Problem 4 (integral representation).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to provide a similar
+   representation of $D(f \Vert g_s^{(\alpha)})$ as an integral, using (17)."
+   **No later source located. Finite-variance Cauchy case proved** in
+   Theorem `thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation` of this manuscript;
+   the general symmetric-stable question remains open in the searched record.
+
+3. **Johnson, Open Problem 6 (remove symmetry).** Exact quote:
+   "Finally, it would be of interest to extend all this work to
+   more general (non-symmetric) families of stable laws, removing restrictions on the
+   parameterization made in Definition 2.1." **No later source located.**
+
+## Machinery-to-Problem Map
+
+- Problem 1: the paper has translate-mixture quotients and the two-solution
+  Bregman derivative (`prop:compact-window-bregman-identity`), but no MMSE
+  score convolution formula. The missing object is precisely a conditional
+  projection identity for Johnson's $\rho^M$; none of the Laurent, tail-energy,
+  or RKHS estimates supplies it.
+- Problem 4: `prop:compact-window-bregman-identity` already differentiates
+  relative entropy for two simultaneous Cauchy semigroup solutions, while
+  `thm:poisson-kl-doob-tail` closes the large-time endpoint. The missing step
+  was to conjugate Johnson's interpolation to
+  $(P_q*\mu,P_q*P_s)$ and close the $q\downarrow0$ endpoint. The new theorem
+  proves exactly that for every finite-variance input, with extended-valued
+  relative entropy allowed.
+- Problem 6: the stable-kernel theorems use isotropic symmetric densities and
+  the Bregman proof uses a symmetric jump kernel. A skew-stable heat kernel,
+  its nonsymmetric generator/adjoint pairing, and replacement domain bounds
+  are all missing. Symmetry is structural in the current proof, not cosmetic.
+
+## Routes B, C, and D
+
+- **B (standard objects):** the canonical standard-object map is the exact
+  dilation conjugacy between Johnson's Cauchy interpolation and the Cauchy
+  convolution semigroup. The Cayley chart also maps the Cauchy law to Haar
+  measure, but the resulting Laurent modes remain computational machinery,
+  not a separate standard-object theorem. The isotropic stable heat kernels
+  in the moment-threshold theorem are already standard objects.
+- **C (hypotheses):** finite variance is used to obtain a compact quotient
+  range and the $q\to\infty$ endpoint in the new proof. It may be stronger
+  than necessary, but removing it requires a finite-entropy domain theorem
+  beyond the present cutoff argument. Symmetry/isotropy is essential to the
+  current Green pairing. Regular variation is essential only for the stated
+  missing-top-moment boundary limit, not for the law-by-law stable tail
+  decomposition.
+- **D (sharpness/converses):** the paper already has a matching counterexample
+  below the uniform stable moment exponent and an iff tail-energy criterion.
+  The plausible unclosed converse is the higher-order analytic moment
+  hierarchy; the nonzero formal top moment proves polynomial-domain
+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.
+
+## Selection
+
+Route A, Johnson Open Problem 4, has the best probability-impact product
+because the required flow is canonically present and both endpoints can be
+closed. The proved result is explicitly the finite-variance Cauchy case, not
+a solution of the full symmetric $\alpha$-stable problem. Problems 1 and 6
+require machinery absent from the paper.

+\begin{theorem}[Cauchy case of Johnson's integral-representation problem]%
+\label{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+Fix \(s>0\), and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\RR\) with finite
+second moment.  For \(q>0\) put
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\qquad u_q=h_q/g_q,
+\]
+and define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
+\[
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+:=\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2\setminus\{x=y\}}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(u_q(x),u_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\dd x\dd y .
+\]
+Then \(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\) is locally integrable on \((0,\infty)\), and,
+with relative entropy between probability measures interpreted in
+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).  Whenever Johnson's score pairing
+in his equation~(17) is defined, comparison with
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} identifies that pairing
+with the displayed nonnegative Bregman density after the change of variables.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their \(x\)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point \(x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing inequality
+give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  For all large \(q\),
+\((1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2\ge(1+y^2)/3\), and
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\).  This identity therefore gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let \(T\to\infty\), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}
+
 \begin{remark}[Tail-integral coefficient transfer]
 \label{rem:no-pointwise-dissipation-from-finite-moments}
 The coefficient transfer below is formulated for tail integrals

+\]
+This follows from the exact dilation conjugacy
+\(q=st/(1-t)\) for Johnson's interpolation
+\((1-t)X+tZ_s\).  The statement is restricted to \(\alpha=1\) and does not
+claim the general symmetric-stable problem.
 \end{maintheorem}

+# Tier-2 Named-Problem Audit
+
+Checked 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore). The primary printed source is
+O. T. Johnson, *A de Bruijn identity for symmetric stable laws*,
+arXiv:1310.2045 (2013), Section 7, pp. 16--17. The arXiv source and PDF were
+both inspected. Searches covered the arXiv API and full search, Crossref,
+the Semantic Scholar and zbMATH records/forward citations already inspected
+in the 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 passes recorded in `literature_check.md`,
+and exact-title/phrase queries for later stable-MMSE, de Bruijn, and
+nonsymmetric-stable entropy work. The live Semantic Scholar endpoint returned
+HTTP 429 and the live zbMATH endpoint returned HTTP 422 in this pass; those
+failures are not represented as successful searches. No later source located
+in the completed searches claims to settle any of the three questions below.
+This is evidence of current status, not a proof of absence from all literature.
+The deceptively close title M. Hirata, A. Nemoto, and H. Yoshida, *An Integral
+Representation of the Relative Entropy*, Entropy 14 (2012), 1469--1477,
+DOI 10.3390/e14081469, was also checked: its abstract and theorem regime are
+Gaussian heat flow, not Johnson's stable interpolation.
+
+## Three Printed Open Problems
+
+1. **Johnson, Open Problem 1 (MMSE-score projection).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to prove a corresponding result for the MMSE score
+   $\rho^M$ of Definition 3.1." Here "corresponding" refers to the
+   preceding conditional-expectation (projection) identity for the Fisher
+   score. **No later source located.**
+
+2. **Johnson, Open Problem 4 (integral representation).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to provide a similar
+   representation of $D(f \Vert g_s^{(\alpha)})$ as an integral, using (17)."
+   **No later source located. Finite-variance Cauchy case proved** in
+   Theorem `thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation` of this manuscript;
+   the general symmetric-stable question remains open in the searched record.
+
+3. **Johnson, Open Problem 6 (remove symmetry).** Exact quote:
+   "Finally, it would be of interest to extend all this work to
+   more general (non-symmetric) families of stable laws, removing restrictions on the
+   parameterization made in Definition 2.1." **No later source located.**
+
+## Machinery-to-Problem Map
+
+- Problem 1: the paper has translate-mixture quotients and the two-solution
+  Bregman derivative (`prop:compact-window-bregman-identity`), but no MMSE
+  score convolution formula. The missing object is precisely a conditional
+  projection identity for Johnson's $\rho^M$; none of the Laurent, tail-energy,
+  or RKHS estimates supplies it.
+- Problem 4: `prop:compact-window-bregman-identity` already differentiates
+  relative entropy for two simultaneous Cauchy semigroup solutions, while
+  `thm:poisson-kl-doob-tail` closes the large-time endpoint. The missing step
+  was to conjugate Johnson's interpolation to
+  $(P_q*\mu,P_q*P_s)$ and close the $q\downarrow0$ endpoint. The new theorem
+  proves exactly that for every finite-variance input, with extended-valued
+  relative entropy allowed.
+- Problem 6: the stable-kernel theorems use isotropic symmetric densities and
+  the Bregman proof uses a symmetric jump kernel. A skew-stable heat kernel,
+  its nonsymmetric generator/adjoint pairing, and replacement domain bounds
+  are all missing. Symmetry is structural in the current proof, not cosmetic.
+
+## Routes B, C, and D
+
+- **B (standard objects):** the canonical standard-object map is the exact
+  dilation conjugacy between Johnson's Cauchy interpolation and the Cauchy
+  convolution semigroup. The Cayley chart also maps the Cauchy law to Haar
+  measure, but the resulting Laurent modes remain computational machinery,
+  not a separate standard-object theorem. The isotropic stable heat kernels
+  in the moment-threshold theorem are already standard objects.
+- **C (hypotheses):** finite variance is used to obtain a compact quotient
+  range and the $q\to\infty$ endpoint in the new proof. It may be stronger
+  than necessary, but removing it requires a finite-entropy domain theorem
+  beyond the present cutoff argument. Symmetry/isotropy is essential to the
+  current Green pairing. Regular variation is essential only for the stated
+  missing-top-moment boundary limit, not for the law-by-law stable tail
+  decomposition.
+- **D (sharpness/converses):** the paper already has a matching counterexample
+  below the uniform stable moment exponent and an iff tail-energy criterion.
+  The plausible unclosed converse is the higher-order analytic moment
+  hierarchy; the nonzero formal top moment proves polynomial-domain
+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.
+
+## Selection
+
+Route A, Johnson Open Problem 4, has the best probability-impact product
+because the required flow is canonically present and both endpoints can be
+closed. The proved result is explicitly the finite-variance Cauchy case, not
+a solution of the full symmetric $\alpha$-stable problem. Problems 1 and 6
+require machinery absent from the paper.

+\begin{theorem}[Cauchy case of Johnson's integral-representation problem]%
+\label{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+Fix \(s>0\), and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\RR\) with finite
+second moment.  For \(q>0\) put
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\qquad u_q=h_q/g_q,
+\]
+and define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
+\[
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+:=\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2\setminus\{x=y\}}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(u_q(x),u_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\dd x\dd y .
+\]
+Then \(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\) is locally integrable on \((0,\infty)\), and,
+with relative entropy between probability measures interpreted in
+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).  Whenever Johnson's score pairing
+in his equation~(17) is defined, comparison with
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} identifies that pairing
+with the displayed nonnegative Bregman density after the change of variables.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their \(x\)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point \(x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing inequality
+give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  For all large \(q\),
+\((1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2\ge(1+y^2)/3\), and
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\).  This identity therefore gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let \(T\to\infty\), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}
+
 \begin{remark}[Tail-integral coefficient transfer]
 \label{rem:no-pointwise-dissipation-from-finite-moments}
 The coefficient transfer below is formulated for tail integrals

+The same domain theorem also resolves the finite-variance Cauchy case of

+\]
+This follows from the exact dilation conjugacy
+\(q=st/(1-t)\) for Johnson's interpolation
+\((1-t)X+tZ_s\).  The statement is restricted to \(\alpha=1\) and does not
+claim the general symmetric-stable problem.
 \end{maintheorem}

+- Problem 1: the paper has translate-mixture quotients and the two-solution
+  Bregman derivative (`prop:compact-window-bregman-identity`), but no MMSE
+  score convolution formula. The missing object is precisely a conditional
+  projection identity for Johnson's $\rho^M$; none of the Laurent, tail-energy,
+  or RKHS estimates supplies it.
+- Problem 4: `prop:compact-window-bregman-identity` already differentiates
+  relative entropy for two simultaneous Cauchy semigroup solutions, while
+  `thm:poisson-kl-doob-tail` closes the large-time endpoint. The missing step
+  was to conjugate Johnson's interpolation to
+  $(P_q*\mu,P_q*P_s)$ and close the $q\downarrow0$ endpoint. The new theorem
+  proves exactly that for every finite-variance input, with extended-valued
+  relative entropy allowed.
+- Problem 6: the stable-kernel theorems use isotropic symmetric densities and
+  the Bregman proof uses a symmetric jump kernel. A skew-stable heat kernel,
+  its nonsymmetric generator/adjoint pairing, and replacement domain bounds
+  are all missing. Symmetry is structural in the current proof, not cosmetic.
+
+## Routes B, C, and D
+
+- **B (standard objects):** the canonical standard-object map is the exact
+  dilation conjugacy between Johnson's Cauchy interpolation and the Cauchy
+  convolution semigroup. The Cayley chart also maps the Cauchy law to Haar
+  measure, but the resulting Laurent modes remain computational machinery,
+  not a separate standard-object theorem. The isotropic stable heat kernels
+  in the moment-threshold theorem are already standard objects.
+- **C (hypotheses):** finite variance is used to obtain a compact quotient
+  range and the $q\to\infty$ endpoint in the new proof. It may be stronger
+  than necessary, but removing it requires a finite-entropy domain theorem
+  beyond the present cutoff argument. Symmetry/isotropy is essential to the
+  current Green pairing. Regular variation is essential only for the stated
+  missing-top-moment boundary limit, not for the law-by-law stable tail
+  decomposition.
+- **D (sharpness/converses):** the paper already has a matching counterexample
+  below the uniform stable moment exponent and an iff tail-energy criterion.
+  The plausible unclosed converse is the higher-order analytic moment
+  hierarchy; the nonzero formal top moment proves polynomial-domain
+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.
+
+## Selection
+
+Route A, Johnson Open Problem 4, has the best probability-impact product
+because the required flow is canonically present and both endpoints can be
+closed. The proved result is explicitly the finite-variance Cauchy case, not
+a solution of the full symmetric $\alpha$-stable problem. Problems 1 and 6
+require machinery absent from the paper.

+\begin{theorem}[Cauchy case of Johnson's integral-representation problem]%
+\label{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+Fix \(s>0\), and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\RR\) with finite
+second moment.  For \(q>0\) put
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\qquad u_q=h_q/g_q,
+\]
+and define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
+\[
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+:=\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2\setminus\{x=y\}}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(u_q(x),u_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\dd x\dd y .
+\]
+Then \(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\) is locally integrable on \((0,\infty)\), and,
+with relative entropy between probability measures interpreted in
+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).  Whenever Johnson's score pairing
+in his equation~(17) is defined, comparison with
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} identifies that pairing
+with the displayed nonnegative Bregman density after the change of variables.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their \(x\)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point \(x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing inequality
+give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  For all large \(q\),
+\((1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2\ge(1+y^2)/3\), and
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\).  This identity therefore gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let \(T\to\infty\), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}
+

 The coefficient transfer below is formulated for tail integrals

+\]

 \end{maintheorem}

+# Tier-2 Named-Problem Audit
+
+Checked 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore). The primary printed source is
+O. T. Johnson, *A de Bruijn identity for symmetric stable laws*,
+arXiv:1310.2045 (2013), Section 7, pp. 16--17. The arXiv source and PDF were
+both inspected. Searches covered the arXiv API and full search, Crossref,
+the Semantic Scholar and zbMATH records/forward citations already inspected
+in the 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 passes recorded in `literature_check.md`,
+and exact-title/phrase queries for later stable-MMSE, de Bruijn, and
+nonsymmetric-stable entropy work. The live Semantic Scholar endpoint returned
+HTTP 429 and the live zbMATH endpoint returned HTTP 422 in this pass; those
+failures are not represented as successful searches. No later source located
+in the completed searches claims to settle any of the three questions below.
+This is evidence of current status, not a proof of absence from all literature.
+The deceptively close title M. Hirata, A. Nemoto, and H. Yoshida, *An Integral
+Representation of the Relative Entropy*, Entropy 14 (2012), 1469--1477,
+DOI 10.3390/e14081469, was also checked: its abstract and theorem regime are
+Gaussian heat flow, not Johnson's stable interpolation.
+
+## Three Printed Open Problems
+
+1. **Johnson, Open Problem 1 (MMSE-score projection).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to prove a corresponding result for the MMSE score
+   $\rho^M$ of Definition 3.1." Here "corresponding" refers to the
+   preceding conditional-expectation (projection) identity for the Fisher
+   score. **No later source located.**
+
+2. **Johnson, Open Problem 4 (integral representation).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to provide a similar
+   representation of $D(f \Vert g_s^{(\alpha)})$ as an integral, using (17)."
+   **No later source located. Finite-variance Cauchy case proved** in
+   Theorem `thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation` of this manuscript;
+   the general symmetric-stable question remains open in the searched record.
+
+3. **Johnson, Open Problem 6 (remove symmetry).** Exact quote:
+   "Finally, it would be of interest to extend all this work to
+   more general (non-symmetric) families of stable laws, removing restrictions on the
+   parameterization made in Definition 2.1." **No later source located.**
+
+## Machinery-to-Problem Map
+
+- Problem 1: the paper has translate-mixture quotients and the two-solution
+  Bregman derivative (`prop:compact-window-bregman-identity`), but no MMSE
+  score convolution formula. The missing object is precisely a conditional
+  projection identity for Johnson's $\rho^M$; none of the Laurent, tail-energy,
+  or RKHS estimates supplies it.
+- Problem 4: `prop:compact-window-bregman-identity` already differentiates
+  relative entropy for two simultaneous Cauchy semigroup solutions, while
+  `thm:poisson-kl-doob-tail` closes the large-time endpoint. The missing step
+  was to conjugate Johnson's interpolation to
+  $(P_q*\mu,P_q*P_s)$ and close the $q\downarrow0$ endpoint. The new theorem
+  proves exactly that for every finite-variance input, with extended-valued
+  relative entropy allowed.
+- Problem 6: the stable-kernel theorems use isotropic symmetric densities and
+  the Bregman proof uses a symmetric jump kernel. A skew-stable heat kernel,
+  its nonsymmetric generator/adjoint pairing, and replacement domain bounds
+  are all missing. Symmetry is structural in the current proof, not cosmetic.
+
+## Routes B, C, and D
+
+- **B (standard objects):** the canonical standard-object map is the exact
+  dilation conjugacy between Johnson's Cauchy interpolation and the Cauchy
+  convolution semigroup. The Cayley chart also maps the Cauchy law to Haar
+  measure, but the resulting Laurent modes remain computational machinery,
+  not a separate standard-object theorem. The isotropic stable heat kernels
+  in the moment-threshold theorem are already standard objects.
+- **C (hypotheses):** finite variance is used to obtain a compact quotient
+  range and the $q\to\infty$ endpoint in the new proof. It may be stronger
+  than necessary, but removing it requires a finite-entropy domain theorem
+  beyond the present cutoff argument. Symmetry/isotropy is essential to the
+  current Green pairing. Regular variation is essential only for the stated
+  missing-top-moment boundary limit, not for the law-by-law stable tail
+  decomposition.
+- **D (sharpness/converses):** the paper already has a matching counterexample
+  below the uniform stable moment exponent and an iff tail-energy criterion.
+  The plausible unclosed converse is the higher-order analytic moment
+  hierarchy; the nonzero formal top moment proves polynomial-domain
+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.
+
+## Selection
+
+Route A, Johnson Open Problem 4, has the best probability-impact product
+because the required flow is canonically present and both endpoints can be
+closed. The proved result is explicitly the finite-variance Cauchy case, not
+a solution of the full symmetric $\alpha$-stable problem. Problems 1 and 6
+require machinery absent from the paper.

+\begin{theorem}[Cauchy case of Johnson's integral-representation problem]%
+\label{thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+Fix \(s>0\), and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\RR\) with finite
+second moment.  For \(q>0\) put
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,\qquad u_q=h_q/g_q,
+\]
+and define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral
+\[
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+:=\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2\setminus\{x=y\}}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(u_q(x),u_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}\dd x\dd y .
+\]
+Then \(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\) is locally integrable on \((0,\infty)\), and,
+with relative entropy between probability measures interpreted in
+\([0,\infty]\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty \mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q .
+\end{equation}
+
+More precisely, let \(X\sim\mu\), let \(Z_s\sim P_s\) be independent, and
+write \(\mu_t\) for the law of Johnson's Cauchy interpolation
+\(X_t=(1-t)X+tZ_s\), \(0\le t<1\).  With
+\[
+q=\frac{st}{1-t},
+\]
+one has
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s}),
+\end{equation}
+and, for almost every \(t\in(0,1)\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative}
+-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(\mu_t\|P_s)
+=\frac{s}{(1-t)^2}
+\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\!\left(\frac{st}{1-t}\right).
+\end{equation}
+Thus \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation} is a nonnegative
+Bregman realization of the integral requested in
+\cite[Open Problem 4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn} for \(\alpha=1\), under the
+stated finite-variance hypothesis.  It does not settle that problem for
+general symmetric stable index \(\alpha\).  Whenever Johnson's score pairing
+in his equation~(17) is defined, comparison with
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} identifies that pairing
+with the displayed nonnegative Bregman density after the change of variables.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Let \(m=\int x\,\mu(\dd x)\), and set
+\[
+A_q(x):=\frac{(P_q*\mu)(x)}{P_q(x-m)},\qquad
+B_q(x):=\frac{P_{q+s}(x)}{P_q(x-m)}.
+\]
+Then \(u_q=A_q/B_q\).  On each compact interval
+\([a,b]\Subset(0,\infty)\), Lemma
+\ref{lem:matched-poisson-quotient-cauchy-bregman-domain} gives one positive
+compact range and one Lipschitz constant for \(A_q\).  Moreover
+\[
+B_q(x)=\frac{q+s}{q}
+\frac{q^2+(x-m)^2}{(q+s)^2+x^2}.
+\]
+The function on the right, its reciprocal, and their \(x\)-derivatives are
+bounded uniformly for \((q,x)\in[a,b]\times\RR\).  Indeed, after adjoining
+the point \(x=\infty\), they are continuous rational functions on the
+compact set \([a,b]\times\overline\RR\), and neither denominator vanishes.
+The quotient rule therefore gives constants
+\(0<c_{a,b}\le C_{a,b}<\infty\) and \(L_{a,b}<\infty\) such that
+\[
+c_{a,b}\le u_q(x)\le C_{a,b},\qquad
+|u_q(x)-u_q(y)|\le L_{a,b}|x-y|.
+\]
+Proposition~\ref{prop:compact-window-bregman-identity}, applied with the two
+initial measures \(\mu\) and \(P_s(x)\dd x\), now shows that
+\[
+H(q):=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_{q+s})
+\]
+is absolutely continuous on \([a,b]\), that
+\(\mathcal J_{\mu,s}\in L^1([a,b])\), and that
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative}
+H'(q)=-\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)
+\quad\text{for a.e. }q\in[a,b].
+\end{equation}
+
+We next close both endpoints separately.  As \(q\downarrow0\),
+\(P_q*\mu\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(P_{q+s}\Rightarrow P_s\).  The variational
+formula for relative entropy gives joint lower semicontinuity under weak
+convergence, whereas convolution by \(P_q\) and the data-processing inequality
+give
+\[
+H(q)=D_{\rm KL}(P_q*\mu\|P_q*P_s)
+\le D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s).
+\]
+Consequently
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-zero-endpoint}
+H(q)\longrightarrow D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+\qquad(q\downarrow0)
+\end{equation}
+in the extended interval \([0,\infty]\).
+
+At the other endpoint, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-moment-density-truncation} with
+\(L=2\) gives \(\|A_q-1\|_\infty=O(q^{-2})\).  If
+\(y=(x-m)/q\), \(\sigma=s/q\), and \(\delta=m/q\), then
+\[
+B_q(x)=(1+\sigma)
+\frac{1+y^2}{(1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2}.
+\]
+The difference of its numerator and denominator is
+\(\sigma y^2-2\delta y-\sigma-\sigma^2-\delta^2\).  For all large \(q\),
+\((1+\sigma)^2+(y+\delta)^2\ge(1+y^2)/3\), and
+\(|y|/(1+y^2)\le1/2\).  This identity therefore gives
+\(\|B_q-1\|_\infty=O((s+|m|)/q)\).  Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:johnson-cauchy-infinity-quotient}
+\|u_q-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
+\end{equation}
+For all large \(q\), the quadratic bound
+\(\Phi(1+r)\le2r^2\) for \(|r|\le1/2\) therefore yields
+\[
+0\le H(q)=\int \Phi(u_q)g_q\dd x
+\le2\|u_q-1\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+
+Integrating \eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} first over a finite
+window gives
+\[
+H(\varepsilon)-H(T)
+=\int_\varepsilon^T\mathcal J_{\mu,s}(q)\dd q.
+\]
+Let \(T\to\infty\), then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and use the two endpoint
+limits and monotone convergence of the nonnegative integral.  This proves
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation}, including when either
+side is infinite.
+
+Finally, dilation by \((1-t)^{-1}\) sends the law of \(X_t\) to
+\[
+\mu*P_{st/(1-t)}=P_q*\mu
+\]
+and sends \(P_s\) to
+\(P_{s/(1-t)}=P_{s+q}\).  Relative entropy is invariant under the same
+bimeasurable dilation of both arguments, proving
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-dilation-conjugacy}.  Since
+\(\dd q/\dd t=s/(1-t)^2\), the chain rule and
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-q-derivative} give
+\eqref{eq:johnson-cauchy-interpolation-derivative} almost everywhere.
+\end{proof}
+

 \label{rem:no-pointwise-dissipation-from-finite-moments}
 The coefficient transfer below is formulated for tail integrals

+The same domain theorem also resolves the finite-variance Cauchy case of
+Johnson's integral-representation problem
+\cite[Open Problem~4]{Johnson2013StableDeBruijn}.  If \(s>0\), \(\mu\) has
+finite second moment, and
+\[
+h_q=P_q*\mu,\qquad g_q=P_{q+s}=P_q*P_s,
+\]
+then the finite-variance Cauchy statement proved in
+\path{sec_doob_phi_entropy.tex} gives
+\[
+D_{\rm KL}(\mu\|P_s)
+=\int_0^\infty\frac1\pi\iint_{\RR^2}
+\frac{g_q(x)\Lambda(h_q(x)/g_q(x),h_q(y)/g_q(y))}{(x-y)^2}
+\dd x\dd y\dd q .
+\]
+This follows from the exact dilation conjugacy
+\(q=st/(1-t)\) for Johnson's interpolation
+\((1-t)X+tZ_s\).  The statement is restricted to \(\alpha=1\) and does not
+claim the general symmetric-stable problem.
 \end{maintheorem}

+# Tier-2 Named-Problem Audit
+
+Checked 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore). The primary printed source is
+O. T. Johnson, *A de Bruijn identity for symmetric stable laws*,
+arXiv:1310.2045 (2013), Section 7, pp. 16--17. The arXiv source and PDF were
+both inspected. Searches covered the arXiv API and full search, Crossref,
+the Semantic Scholar and zbMATH records/forward citations already inspected
+in the 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 passes recorded in `literature_check.md`,
+and exact-title/phrase queries for later stable-MMSE, de Bruijn, and
+nonsymmetric-stable entropy work. The live Semantic Scholar endpoint returned
+HTTP 429 and the live zbMATH endpoint returned HTTP 422 in this pass; those
+failures are not represented as successful searches. No later source located
+in the completed searches claims to settle any of the three questions below.
+This is evidence of current status, not a proof of absence from all literature.
+The deceptively close title M. Hirata, A. Nemoto, and H. Yoshida, *An Integral
+Representation of the Relative Entropy*, Entropy 14 (2012), 1469--1477,
+DOI 10.3390/e14081469, was also checked: its abstract and theorem regime are
+Gaussian heat flow, not Johnson's stable interpolation.
+
+## Three Printed Open Problems
+
+1. **Johnson, Open Problem 1 (MMSE-score projection).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to prove a corresponding result for the MMSE score
+   $\rho^M$ of Definition 3.1." Here "corresponding" refers to the
+   preceding conditional-expectation (projection) identity for the Fisher
+   score. **No later source located.**
+
+2. **Johnson, Open Problem 4 (integral representation).** Exact quote:
+   "It would be of interest to provide a similar
+   representation of $D(f \Vert g_s^{(\alpha)})$ as an integral, using (17)."
+   **No later source located. Finite-variance Cauchy case proved** in
+   Theorem `thm:johnson-cauchy-integral-representation` of this manuscript;
+   the general symmetric-stable question remains open in the searched record.
+
+3. **Johnson, Open Problem 6 (remove symmetry).** Exact quote:
+   "Finally, it would be of interest to extend all this work to
+   more general (non-symmetric) families of stable laws, removing restrictions on the
+   parameterization made in Definition 2.1." **No later source located.**
+
+## Machinery-to-Problem Map
+
+- Problem 1: the paper has translate-mixture quotients and the two-solution
+  Bregman derivative (`prop:compact-window-bregman-identity`), but no MMSE
+  score convolution formula. The missing object is precisely a conditional
+  projection identity for Johnson's $\rho^M$; none of the Laurent, tail-energy,
+  or RKHS estimates supplies it.
+- Problem 4: `prop:compact-window-bregman-identity` already differentiates
+  relative entropy for two simultaneous Cauchy semigroup solutions, while
+  `thm:poisson-kl-doob-tail` closes the large-time endpoint. The missing step
+  was to conjugate Johnson's interpolation to
+  $(P_q*\mu,P_q*P_s)$ and close the $q\downarrow0$ endpoint. The new theorem
+  proves exactly that for every finite-variance input, with extended-valued
+  relative entropy allowed.
+- Problem 6: the stable-kernel theorems use isotropic symmetric densities and
+  the Bregman proof uses a symmetric jump kernel. A skew-stable heat kernel,
+  its nonsymmetric generator/adjoint pairing, and replacement domain bounds
+  are all missing. Symmetry is structural in the current proof, not cosmetic.
+
+## Routes B, C, and D
+
+- **B (standard objects):** the canonical standard-object map is the exact
+  dilation conjugacy between Johnson's Cauchy interpolation and the Cauchy
+  convolution semigroup. The Cayley chart also maps the Cauchy law to Haar
+  measure, but the resulting Laurent modes remain computational machinery,
+  not a separate standard-object theorem. The isotropic stable heat kernels
+  in the moment-threshold theorem are already standard objects.
+- **C (hypotheses):** finite variance is used to obtain a compact quotient
+  range and the $q\to\infty$ endpoint in the new proof. It may be stronger
+  than necessary, but removing it requires a finite-entropy domain theorem
+  beyond the present cutoff argument. Symmetry/isotropy is essential to the
+  current Green pairing. Regular variation is essential only for the stated
+  missing-top-moment boundary limit, not for the law-by-law stable tail
+  decomposition.
+- **D (sharpness/converses):** the paper already has a matching counterexample
+  below the uniform stable moment exponent and an iff tail-energy criterion.
+  The plausible unclosed converse is the higher-order analytic moment
+  hierarchy; the nonzero formal top moment proves polynomial-domain
+  minimality, not necessity for an entropy remainder, and tail cancellation
+  prevents promoting it without new analysis.
+
+## Selection
+
+Route A, Johnson Open Problem 4, has the best probability-impact product
+because the required flow is canonically present and both endpoints can be
+closed. The proved result is explicitly the finite-variance Cauchy case, not
+a solution of the full symmetric $\alpha$-stable problem. Problems 1 and 6
+require machinery absent from the paper.
